name: DocuSign
subcategory: PDF editing, document workflows and electronic signatures
tagline: Request a low-stakes signature with a transparent audit log and no legal-assurance claim

pricing.freeTier: No free plan, just a trial; signing documents sent to you is always free.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.notes: Annual commitment of $132, paid in monthly installments; current month-to-month price was not exposed on the live page.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: Up to 50 users; 100 envelopes/user/year on annual billing.
tiers.notes: Annual commitment of $360/user, paid monthly; the month-to-month option includes 10 envelopes/user/month but its live price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Business Pro
tiers.limits: Up to 50 users; 100 envelopes/user/year on annual billing.
tiers.notes: Annual commitment of $540/user, paid monthly; the month-to-month option includes 10 envelopes/user/month but its live price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Enhanced
tiers.limits: 50+ users and a custom envelope allowance.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free sending tier; recipients can sign without an account; a 30-day free trial is available
pricing.billingTerms: annual commitment billed monthly; month-to-month plans also exist but current public monthly prices were not exposed; auto-renews
pricing.hiddenCosts: A sent envelope counts even if never signed. Standard and Business Pro overages are pay-as-you-go at an undisclosed per-envelope rate; SMS starts at $0.36/delivery and identity verification at $2.40/attempt. Cancelling an annual commitment after 30 days leaves the remaining annual balance, taxes and overages due.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For DocuSign, request a low-stakes signature with a transparent audit log and no legal-assurance claim. The hard boundary is brand trust, identity options, global legal framework, integrations, and compliance, plus document fidelity, identity, and compliance.
coreLoopDIY: Request a low-stakes signature with a transparent audit log, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store without any legal-assurance claim.
whatYouLose: brand trust, identity options, global legal framework, integrations, and compliance
replacementScope: personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow
ongoingBurden: format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for DocuSign because the visible editor is reproducible, but reliable rendering and legally defensible signature workflows are not a casual side project. The recurring cost buys format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Stirling PDF
priorArt.desc: Active open-source web application for a broad set of PDF operations.

alternatives.name: Documenso
alternatives.desc: Open-source document signing with templates, recipients, verification, and audit history; production self-hosting means Postgres, email, HTTPS, and actual operations.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose, Railway or Kubernetes self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Document metadata and audit records in PostgreSQL; PDFs and files in S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It has less mature identity verification, regulatory assurance, enterprise administration and integration coverage than DocuSign.
facts.setupBlocker: Production self-hosting needs PostgreSQL, SMTP, S3-compatible storage, a domain, HTTPS, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: DocuSeal
alternatives.desc: Reusable document templates, multiple recipients, signing links, reminders, and audit records; self-host it and the core workflow is not metered.

facts.install: Hosted signup or one-command Docker or Docker Compose
facts.dataFormat: By default SQLite and uploaded documents in the mounted /data directory; PostgreSQL and MySQL are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not match DocuSign's breadth of identity checks, compliance programs, enterprise controls and integrations.
facts.setupBlocker: Production still needs persistent volumes, a domain, HTTPS, email delivery, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: OpenSign
alternatives.desc: A polished signature-request product with templates, sequential signing, audit trails, and a small hosted free allowance; Docker removes the vendor cap.

facts.dataFormat: Signing data in MongoDB and documents in configured file or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its compliance evidence, identity-verification options, enterprise administration and integration ecosystem are less mature than DocuSign's.
facts.setupBlocker: The sample MongoDB must be made persistent or replaced, then storage, SMTP, domain, HTTPS and backups must be configured

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Personal plan and a personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for DocuSign in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Python 3.12, FastAPI, pikepdf, LibreOffice headless, and PostgreSQL; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: request a low-stakes signature with a transparent audit log, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store without any legal-assurance claim.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Keep every original immutable and write each operation to a versioned output file.
Support merge, split, reorder, rotate, compress, watermark, redact, OCR, and Office-to-PDF conversion.
Render page previews and warn when fonts, forms, signatures, or encryption may be altered.
For signature mode, place fields, invite signers, record consent, and seal a final PDF hash.
Maintain an append-only event log with timestamps, document hashes, and delivery outcomes.
Add file expiry, download, deletion, backup, and a prominent low-stakes-use warning.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out qualified or regulated electronic signatures.
Deliberately leave out government identity verification.
Deliberately leave out full Acrobat-level editing and enterprise document governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
